items.title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy Research & Measurement
items.description: About the Team The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment. About the Role We are hiring a senior applied scientist to study how AI affects people and society using OpenAI production data, experiments, and social science methods. This role sits at the intersection of applied social science, AI, and product policy. The scientist will own research from an ambiguous question through study design, data collection and analysis, methodological validation, and recommendations. Their work will inform product and policy decisions and, where appropriate, contribute to external publications. We are looking for a hands-on empirical social scientist with exceptional methodological judgment. In this role, you will: - Develop and execute a research agenda on AI’s social impact, including effects on well-being, learning, social connection, trust, and human decision-making, in partnership with product and policy teams. - Own empirical studies end to end: define the question and estimand, choose the design, build the dataset, conduct the analysis, and explain what the evidence supports. - Analyze large-scale production and behavioral data, linking them to experiments, surveys, or external outcomes when appropriate to measure real-world effects. - Design randomized experiments and credible observational studies; test identification assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and distinguish association from causal effects. - Develop and validate measures of social outcomes, including human and LLM-assisted annotations; assess measurement error, subgroup performance, and drift. - Translate findings into concrete product and policy recommendations, with clear limits on causal interpretation, generalizability, and decision confidence. - Partner with Product Policy, Research, Product, Data Science, Engineering, UXR, Legal, and domain experts; contribute rigorous work to external publications when appropriate. You might thrive in this role if you have: - A PhD or equivalent research experience in sociology, political science, psychology, communication, computational social science, or a related empirical field, with demonstrated independent research ownership. - Deep expertise in research design, causal inference, experimentation, statistical analysis, and measurement, demonstrated through work you can personally explain and defend. - Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with experience independently constructing and analyzing complex behavioral datasets and producing reproducible research. - A record of research that informs consequential decisions about technology and people, with the judgment to identify both useful findings and unresolved uncertainty. - Clear writing for technical and policy audiences, and experience producing rigorous research papers or equivalent public technical work. - The ability to move quickly, collaborate across functions, and maintain scientific independence when findings are sensitive or inconvenient. items.title: Corporate Counsel, Public Reporting
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role We are looking for an experienced securities lawyer to join the Corporate Legal team as Corporate Counsel, Public Company Reporting & Governance. In this role, you will prepare our SEC filings, advise on securities law and corporate governance, and support the Board and its committees. You will also partner closely with finance, accounting, investor relations, and equity teams to build the systems, controls, and repeatable processes that accurate, timely disclosure depends on. This is a hands-on role with meaningful scope and visibility. You will provide strategic, practical advice to senior leaders and teams across the company. You will draft and review disclosure yourself, while also helping build the processes and workflows that allow the function to scale. Key Responsibilities Prepare and review SEC filings, including Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K, the proxy statement and Section 16 filings Advise on compliance with SEC and Nasdaq rules Help establish and run our disclosure controls and procedures, including the disclosure committee and the reporting calendar Support our securities compliance policies and the administration of the Insider Trading Policy, including trading windows, pre-clearance and 10b5-1 plans Review earnings materials, press releases, investor presentations and other significant external and internal communications Partner with Investor Relations on Regulation FD compliance, stockholder engagement and the annual meeting Prepare Board and committee materials, draft minutes and resolutions, and maintain governance policies and committee charters Support executive and equity compensation disclosure with the People and Equity teams Advise the teams that report publicly on our mission and safety work Keep partner teams informed of governance trends and SEC and Nasdaq developments Contribute to the processes and tools that let a small team handle public company work at scale Minimum Qualifications Hold a law degree (JD, LLB, or equivalent) and meet the local licensing requirements to work as in-house counsel where you’ll be based (California or New York preferred) Significant public company reporting experience. This role is focused on periodic reporting and governance, and is not a capital markets or M&A role Deep knowledge of corporate and securities law, including SEC and Nasdaq rules Experience giving accurate, practical advice in real time at a fast-growing company A working understanding of accounting and corporate finance A track record of building strong working relationships across teams Clear written and verbal communication with executives and non-lawyers, without legal jargon Preferred Qualifications At least 8 years of relevant legal experience, including securities and corporate governance experience at a law firm and in-house at a public company Experience building processes and procedures to public-company standards Experience supporting a public company board and its committees A track record of standing up a process or program The ability to translate securities law requirements into clear, practical guidance for business teams Sound judgment and the ability to advise with incomplete information Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or New York office at least 3 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $335,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The HRBP team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path isn’t always obvious. We stay close to the business so we understand its realities, and focus our time where judgment, influence, and context can make the biggest difference: improving decisions, strengthening leaders, and helping teams work better. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Go-to-Market HR Business Partner, you’ll be a trusted advisor, sounding board, and hands-on problem solver for leaders in your client group. This is an individual contributor role. You’ll help leaders decide how to organize, grow, and lead their teams, bringing a point of view on the tradeoffs rather than simply executing the first request. That starts with understanding the business problem. If customer coverage needs to change, for example, you’ll help leaders clarify what’s driving the change, weigh options for team structure and staffing, and work with them to put the decision into practice. The goal is to leave leaders better equipped to make the next decision, too. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Help GTM leaders make better decisions about team structure, workforce plans, and hiring. Work with Finance and Recruiting to turn those decisions into plans the business can execute. - Build leadership capability by giving candid, actionable feedback and coaching managers through complex performance, development, and succession decisions. - Lead the people side of organizational changes, from planning and communication to clarifying roles and supporting teams through transitions. - Work with regional HRBPs and People partners, including Compensation and Employee Relations, to apply consistent practices while accounting for local needs. - Use workforce data, employee feedback, and business context to spot issues early, test assumptions, and track progress. - Build simple systems and routines that help GTM teams scale. Improve how leaders review talent, spot emerging issues, and follow through on decisions. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have partnered with senior leaders as an HRBP in a fast-growing technology organization, with direct experience supporting Sales, Revenue, Customer Success, or a related GTM function. - Understand how customer-facing teams are structured and how shifts in growth, customer coverage, or operating models affect what those teams need. - Have led org design, workforce planning, talent reviews, or significant organizational change and can show how you turned a plan into action. - Build trust quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and influence decisions without relying on formal authority. - Build trust with senior leaders, ask questions that get to the root of the problem, and challenge assumptions with care. items.title: Certification Architect
items.description: About the Team Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption. Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability. About the Role As Certification Architect, you will define the framework, standards, and assessment architecture that make OpenAI certifications a trusted signal of demonstrated capability. This is a senior hands-on role on the Certification team that will build reusable foundations for a growing portfolio: clear competency standards, defensible assessments, scalable in-product delivery, and evidence of continued competence. We’re looking for someone who combines deep certification and assessment expertise with the ability to innovate new and meaningful ways to demonstrate practical AI competence. You will work closely with certification specialists, technical subject matter experts, learning product and engineering teams, operations and policy partners, and stakeholders across the go-to-market organization. The program is early, and you will help shape how people demonstrate capability in ChatGPT and Codex. Success means building standards that are rigorous, usable, and adaptable as AI technology and professional roles evolve. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Own the credential framework and shared competency standards, distinguishing completed learning, demonstrated skills, and formal certification, with clear capability claims and evidence requirements for each. - Establish reusable assessment standards and guidance for certification pods across job-task analysis, competency models, assessment blueprints, performance tasks, scoring rubrics, and passing standards. - Own the validation approach and evidence documentation requirements. Partner with pod leaders to validate certification proposals against job relevance, representative task coverage, scoring consistency, fairness, and appropriate interpretation of results. - Define exam delivery architecture and requirements with product, engineering, operations, and third parties, spanning registration, identity verification, monitoring, permitted assistance, evidence capture, scoring, human review, appeals, customer support, and record management. - Define expectations for continued competence validation post-assessment. - Partner with learning, operations, policy, legal, privacy, security, and accessibility teams to align preparation with competencies while protecting assessment integrity and establishing appropriate evidence access, retention, accommodations, and review processes. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 10+ years experience designing and delivering professional technical IT industry certifications or assessments that support credible claims about what people can do. - Have led design of performance-based assessments for AI, software development, technical architecture, or customer-facing implementation roles. - Required: Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs. - Have built credential frameworks, competency models, or shared assessment standards that work across multiple roles or programs. - Have led job-task analysis, assessment blueprints, performance-based assessment, rubric design, standard setting, and the evidence needed to support valid and fair certification decisions. - Can translate assessment experience requirements into exam delivery specifications for third parties and learning product teams. - Have worked closely with certification specialists, psychometricians and subject matter experts to validate assessment and scoring standards and improve assessment quality. - Communicate complex standards clearly to technical and nontechnical partners, and build alignment across teams without relying on formal authority. - Enjoy hands-on work, from drafting standards and reviewing assessment designs to resolving practical delivery tradeoffs with a small team. - Exercise sound judgment in ambiguous environments, balancing rigor, candidate experience, delivery feasibility, and the pace of technology change. - Care deeply about accessibility, fairness, and the integrity of credentials that individuals and employers rely on. - Build reusable approaches while recognizing where different roles need distinct competency models, tasks, and evidence. It’s a plus if you have experience: - Validating AI-assisted scoring, model evaluations, or other automated approaches to evaluating human performance. - Working with secure assessment delivery, identity verification, credential issuance, learner records, or assessment technology providers. - Developing innovative approaches to recertification, ongoing competence, or assessment of authentic work. - Building products that serve both individual users and organizations. items.title: Technical Program Manager, Life Sciences Research (Genetic Medicine)
items.location_text: Boston, MA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Thousands of rare genetic diseases have a known cause but no approved treatment. Advances in gene editing and oligonucleotide medicines have made it possible to design therapies for very small populations, sometimes for a single patient, but developing them remains slow and costly. Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is exploring how frontier AI, combined with deep drug development expertise and strong external partnerships, can help change that. We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to bring structure and momentum to this work. You’ll coordinate across programs that support the development of individualized genetic medicines, advance research into new therapeutic approaches, and help patient organizations, non-profits, and researchers use Claude in their own rare disease work. You’ll partner closely with scientists, engineers, clinicians, and external collaborators to keep complex efforts moving toward shared milestones. Much of this work remains in early stages, so this is a foundational role on a small team. You’ll help define how the team operates, build the plans and processes that allow it to grow, and work with our researchers and engineers to find where Claude can be most useful. If you’ve run complex programs in drug development or clinical research and want to help advance treatments for rare disease, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Build and own an integrated program plan, including milestones, dependencies, risks, budgets, and key decisions Coordinate with clinical, manufacturing, and research partners on programs that span preclinical development, manufacturing, regulatory review, and clinical care Run the operating cadence with external partners, tracking progress and raising risks early Work with Legal, Finance, and Partnerships to turn agreements into clear operating plans and track commitments Coordinate research across internal scientists, academic collaborators, companies, and contract research organizations, helping to scope projects, sequence work, and support timely decisions Help ensure that data is shared responsibly and in a usable form, with appropriate consent, privacy protections, and data-sharing agreements in place Lead programs that support non-profits, patient organizations, and academic and independent researchers, from onboarding through ongoing support and feedback Help connect genetic diagnosis efforts with therapeutic research and development Share insights from partners and programs with Anthropic’s research and product teams to help improve Claude for scientific and medical research Write clear status updates, risk assessments, and decision memos, and build processes that scale with the team Minimum qualifications Experience as a technical program manager or program lead on complex drug development, clinical research, or translational science programs involving multiple external organizations, such as manufacturers, contract research organizations, or clinical sites Working knowledge of how a therapy moves from preclinical development into the clinic, including manufacturing, regulatory filings, and clinical operations, and how a delay in one stage affects the others Scientific fluency in molecular biology or genetics, sufficient to follow experimental plans, review data with scientists, and understand tradeoffs Strong program management skills, including project planning, milestones, risk registers, budget tracking, and dependency management across many concurrent workstreams A track record of driving work to completion across organizations without formal authority Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to make complex scientific and operational issues easy to understand and act on Comfort working with ambiguity and building process where none exists Excitement about Anthropic’s mission to build safe and beneficial AI Preferred qualifications An advanced degree in a life science, engineering, or related field Experience with gene therapy, gene editing, or oligonucleotide programs, especially individualized (N-of-1) or ultra-rare disease programs Clinical operations experience, such as multi-site trials, master protocols, IRB submissions, or site activation Experience managing sponsored research agreements, grants, or philanthropic funding with academic institutions Experience working with patient advocacy groups, rare disease foundations, or other non-profits Familiarity with clinical genomics and genetic diagnosis Experience with patient data governance, including consent, HIPAA, and data-sharing agreements Experience in a role that bridges software or AI and the life sciences Experience as an early hire on a new team, helping define how it operates Hands-on experience using LLM tools like Claude in your day-to-day work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $290,000 — $365,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As GTM Narrative Lead at Anthropic, you will be the keeper of Anthropic's company story for customers. You will own the company narrative presentation end to end and keep it current as models and products ship, shaping how customers first hear who Anthropic is, what Claude changes for them, and why we are the right partner. This is a hands-on individual contributor role in Solutions & Segment Marketing, within Enterprise Marketing. You will shape the storyline with senior leaders and write the words, the script, and the deck yourself. You will work closely with Product Marketing, Product, Research, Sales, Enablement, Brand, Design, and Communications to translate complex AI capabilities into compelling stories that resonate with enterprise buyers and reflect Anthropic's commitment to developing AI systems that are safe, steerable, and beneficial. What you'll be shaping Your narrative will be the starting point for customer conversations across executives, sellers, partners, and events. Each model and product launch changes what customers can do, and you will work directly with the people building it to turn it into a story a CEO can act on. You will also set up how the work gets done: the customer-insight loop, the measures, and the Claude workflows that keep a story current at this pace. This role offers the opportunity to shape how one of the world's leading AI companies tells its story at a pivotal moment in the industry's development, while ensuring our narrative reflects our commitment to responsible AI deployment and societal benefit. Key responsibilities Own the company narrative: Own Anthropic's company narrative presentation from start to finish, including the storyline, the master deck, speaker notes, and the versions used by executives, sales, partners, and events Translate capabilities into customer outcomes: Turn complex research and product capabilities into a clear story about what changes for customers, what it's worth, and why Anthropic is the right partner Keep the story current through every launch: Lead the narrative update for every major launch, so the story is refreshed, approved, and in the hands of the field on launch day Build and run a customer-insight loop: Use win/loss reviews, call recordings, executive briefings, customer advisory input, and usage data to keep testing and adjusting the storyline Drive cross-functional alignment: Partner with Product Marketing, Brand, Design, and Communications to keep the company narrative aligned with positioning, messaging, and external voice Measure whether the narrative works: Define and report on how widely the deck is used, how often key messages show up in deals, and feedback from customers and executives Build workflows with Claude: Speed up research, customer feedback summaries, drafting, and versioning Minimum qualifications A storytelling background in corporate messaging, brand, communications, speechwriting, content, or product marketing, with a track record of personally writing a company, brand, or portfolio-level narrative. Consumer and B2B backgrounds are both welcome Recent, hands-on writing of the story itself, such as scripts, speeches, keynotes, or a master deck, including speaker notes and audience versions Proven ability to turn complex or technical subject matter into a story that moves its audience, whether consumers, executives, or business buyers Experience leading narrative updates for major launches on short timelines, through review and into the field Experience using audience or customer insight (research, feedback, call recordings, usage data) to test a story and change it Experience measuring narrative use and impact, and reporting it to leadership Experience aligning Product Marketing, Brand, Design, and Communications around one story without formal authority Regular use of AI tools for research, synthesis, drafting, or versioning Creative range and a distinctive voice, with a willingness to break from standard enterprise messaging conventions Curiosity and ability to learn a technical product quickly, even without a technical or enterprise software background Executive presence, with comfort presenting the story to customers and senior leaders Preferred qualifications 15+ years of experience in corporate messaging, brand, communications, content, or product marketing at technology companies or consumer brands - a blend of experience at technology startups and scaled technology companies is strongly preferred Experience owning an AI story or message, or marketing AI, cloud, data, or developer platforms Experience at a company where the product changed constantly and content had a short shelf life Speechwriting, keynote, or executive briefing writing experience Time spent in or close to sales, field marketing, or enablement Experience in a regulated or high-trust category where safety and security are part of the story Experience on a brand, content, communications, or PR team at a consumer technology company or brand during a defining cultural moment, where the story had to reach and move a broad audience Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or New York office at least 2 days a week. We encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $400,000 — $570,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Enterprise Go-To-Market organization helps the world’s largest companies adopt and scale our AI platform across their business from ChatGPT Enterprise to our developer platform and APIs. We partner with organizations across the enterprise to build new AI-powered customer experiences, transform operations, and reimagine how work gets done in highly regulated and technically complex environments. As adoption accelerates through pilots, experimentation, and developer-led use cases, the GTM team turns that momentum into durable, enterprise-wide deployments. Account Associates sit at the front of this motion where technical curiosity turns into executive engagement, and early product signals become enterprise-wide deployments. ABOUT THE ROLE As an Account Associate, you’ll help our Enterprise teams turn product usage, pilots, inbound interest, and targeted outreach into qualified enterprise opportunities. Working alongside Account Directors, you’ll apply your sales experience to discovery, stakeholder mapping, and account strategy while deepening your ability to navigate complex enterprise opportunities. You’ll exercise judgment in handling discovery and qualification assignments, evaluating differing stakeholder needs and recommending next steps while drawing on Account Directors for guidance on more complex issues. We are looking for individuals with 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both. Candidates should be motivated to build on that experience and grow into world-class enterprise sellers. This role can lead to opportunities as an Account Director or in other GTM roles, with progression based on performance and business needs rather than a fixed timeline. For the right person, this is an opportunity to build on an established sales foundation and develop a long-term career in AI go-to-market. This role is based in Austin, TX. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week (Monday through Wednesday) and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Partner with Account Directors on account strategy, multi-threading, and deal progression. Assess account developments and recommend adjustments to engagement approaches within agreed priorities. - Design and execute targeted outbound strategies using industry context, stakeholder mapping, and product signal to break into priority accounts. - Lead high-quality discovery to uncover business priorities, map stakeholders, and assess enterprise readiness. Evaluate differing stakeholder needs and incomplete information to recommend qualification decisions and next steps. - Contribute to pipeline reviews by sharing outbound activity, account insights, and early competitive signals. - Build and iterate on AI-enabled GTM workflows (GPTs/agents) to scale prospecting and qualification. YOU MAY THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have 2–4 years of professional sales experience in SDR/BDR roles, full-cycle Account Executive roles, or a combination of both, with demonstrated success in your assigned responsibilities. Experience working at a startup or selling enterprise SaaS is strongly preferred. - Have a track record of meeting or exceeding quota or measurable sales targets, such as qualified pipeline, sales opportunities, or revenue, with clear examples of your individual contribution. - Demonstrate strong business acumen and can lead discovery conversations that uncover customer priorities, connect potential solutions to measurable outcomes, and establish clear next steps. - Have experience researching accounts, developing targeted outreach, and engaging business and technical stakeholders to generate qualified opportunities. Experience prospecting into enterprise or strategic accounts is a plus. - Have a strong interest in AI, regularly experiment with AI tools, and can connect their capabilities to practical business needs. - Use performance data and feedback to refine your approach, and show persistence when outreach or opportunities do not progress as expected. - Are comfortable with ambiguity, moving quickly, and taking ownership of your work while collaborating closely with Account Directors. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy https://cdn.openai.com/policies/global-employee-and-contractor-privacy-policy.pdf At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

items.title: Corporate Finance Intern (Summer 2027)
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Corporate Finance team’s mission is to generate accurate and actionable insights for leadership regarding business performance, and communicate them in a way that empowers strategic decision making. We own the company’s consolidated financial picture, including forecasting, planning, and reporting. We translate operating activity into the financial narrative that leadership, the Board, and investors rely on. As the business scales, the team keeps sharpening how we understand and explain performance across Robinhood’s product suite. As a Corporate Finance Intern, you will join the team during forecast cycles and work with stakeholders across Brokerage, Crypto, and Money. You will help turn granular data into the clear takeaways senior leadership needs to make strategic decisions. You will also contribute to the team’s consolidated model and the reporting used across the Finance org to track key performance indicators. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Program Lead, GFCO Performance & Enablement on the CX Compliance Operations team, you’ll build the learning and performance programs that keep our financial crime investigations accurate, consistent, and audit ready. The team delivers Transaction Monitoring, Enhanced Due Diligence, Screening, and Complaints Investigations, so readiness for complex regulated cases matters from day one. You’ll own programs from needs analysis through evaluation, and your work will show up in investigation quality, case handling efficiency, and regulatory readiness. Design practical learning experiences, including facilitated sessions, self-paced content, job aids, scenario-based practice, and assessments grounded in approved compliance procedures. Experience building practical learning content such as facilitated sessions, self-paced modules, assessments, and job aids with learning platforms and authoring tools, including validating AI-generated content against authoritative sources. Consistent success partnering cross-functionally without formal authority, including challenging unclear requirements and communicating trade-offs plainly. Our businesses — Fanatics Commerce, Fanatics Collectibles, Fanatics Betting & Gaming, Fanatics Events, Fanatics Advertising, Fanatics Markets and Fanatics Studios — maximize the presence and reach for hundreds of partners globally and create a one-stop experience that allows fans to buy, bet, collect, and earn, while engaging with sports in deeper, more immersive ways. This includes licensed fan gear and lifestyle products, sportsbook and iGaming, physical and digital trading cards, live events, premium sports entertainment content, credit card offerings and more. Together, they form a powerful, integrated ecosystem — connected by the Fanatics ONE loyalty program and FanCash, the currency of sport — delivering personalized experiences to over 100 million fans worldwide. Fanatics holds partnerships with over 900 sports properties, from professional leagues and players’ associations to teams, colleges and retail partners; over 7,000 athletes and celebrities; and over 2,000 retail locations, including all Lids stores. Backed by a team of more than 22,000 employees, Fanatics is committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience. The Role The Travel Logistics Associate is the systems, budget, and organization backbone of travel for talent attending Fanatics Fest, on behalf of the Talent Operations / Content team. Working directly for the Talent Ops Manager, this role owns the Airtable source of truth for travel, onboards and organizes the contracted travel managers, tracks the travel budget, and works with vendors to make sure they are paid and operating efficiently. The associate is the liaison between the Talent Ops Manager, travel managers, and vendors, flagging major changes promptly. They keep the data organized so the team can back up its decisions and support cross-company charging post-event. Travel experience is helpful but not required. We are hiring first for an organized systems project manager with a strong budget focus and attention to detail. What You'll Do Systems & Airtable Ownership Own and maintain the Airtable travel tracker as the single source of truth for travel managers, hotels, vendors, and logistics Keep all contracted travel managers organized and working from current, accurate information which is changing rapidly Maintain an organized running list of outstanding information and blockers and follow up persistently with all parties to close items out on time Travel Manager & Vendor Coordination Partner with the Finance Manager to onboard all contracted travel managers ahead of the event Support travel manager training with the Talent Ops Manager and complete all system access and admin setup for travel managers ahead of the event Serve as the onsite point person for contracted travel managers throughout the event Act as the liaison between the Talent Ops Manager, travel managers, and vendors, communicating any major changes promptly Work with vendors to ensure they are paid on time and to identify efficiencies, such as hotel check-in vacancies and repurposing any open rooms Work with vendors and the Content team on final reconciliations, including budget and cross-company charging Hotel & Ground Logistics Coordinate with On Location team on information for hotel blocks and maintain working knowledge of existing hotel inventory to keep content and talent ops team up to date and ensuring proper allocations Own end-to-end hotel logistics for staff, vendors, and talent, including rooming lists, tracking, stakeholder communications, and real-time updates as plans change Track ground transportation and car logistics, both pre-event and onsite, in partnership with the travel managers and vendors and reporting up to Talent Ops mgr Budget & Financial Administration Manage travel budget tracking and reconciliation, partnering closely with the Content team Manage P-card activity and receipt submission on a timely, ongoing basis Cross-Functional Partnership with Content Join Content team booking calls to understand ownership and cost division of talent costs Partner directly with the Content team under leadership of the talent ops mgr to align travel schedules with talent schedules and daily changes Scope & Escalations This role does not book travel and does not work directly with travel agents. The contracted travel managers handle bookings and agent communications. Any escalations go to the Talent Ops Manager, content team and relationship stakeholders. This travel logistics coordinator is the first line of defense to trouble shoot before escalations go up the chain. What We're Looking For Experience in project management, operations, production coordination, travel coordination, or a related role; prior travel experience is a plus but not required Airtable skills preferred but not required, eagerness to learn and proficient in excel, tracking and project management are key Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple travel managers, vendors, and deadlines simultaneously Comfortable owning budget tracking, expense reconciliation, and P-card administration Clear, proactive communicator able to partner cross-functionally with Content, vendors, and travel managers, and to flag changes quickly Calm and steady in a fast-moving event environment Proficiency with Airtable, Claude integrations, Excel/Google Sheets, and expense management tools preferred but not required Eager and willing to work in a fast paced, high stakes but fun environment! Reporting & Onboarding This role reports to and works under the guidance of the Talent Ops Manager. In the lead-up to the program, the Talent Ops Manager will support onboarding and training and help liaise with the Content team and other stakeholders until this person is fully up to speed on process and able to operate slightly more independently. The salary range represents base pay only and does not include short-term or long-term incentive compensation. When determining base pay as part of a final compensation package, we consider several factors such as location, experience, qualifications, and training. For information about our benefits, please visit https://benefitsatfanatics.com/ Salary Range $70,000 — $80,000 USD By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our Candidate Privacy Policy. Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process. If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Fanatics recruiting, please do not respond and report it here .

items.title: Application Security Engineer - Agents platform
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE ElevenAgents is our platform for building and running conversational AI agents at scale. As our first Application Security Engineer embedded in the Agents team, you’ll make the secure way the easy way. You’ll build the security tooling and reusable primitives that let engineers ship securely by default. This is a builder role. Expect to spend about 70% of your time building tools and internal systems, and the rest working with engineers, staying in sync with Core Security, and doing security research. More than half of the work is greenfield and most of it starts with you, you’ll spot the problems worth solving and own each solution from idea to production. You will: - Build security primitives that are easy for engineers to adopt, starting from what you find when you audit the Agents codebase - Review new product work for security and feed what you learn back into shared tooling - Lead the major security improvements to the Agents platform, working closely with Core Security - Make sure Agents platform uses authn and authz controls correctly and building the guardrails that keep the platform from compromising on security best practices - Set the security bar for the Agents platform and make meeting it the easy path for product engineers - Work with engineers daily to help them ship fast and safely REQUIREMENTS - 5+ years in application security engineering at scale, covering secure design, vulnerability management and security tooling - Strong software engineering skills: you have built and shipped products end to end, in production-quality code - Fluency in Python, our main language. Golang or another language is fine if you can pick up Python quickly - Hands-on experience with authentication and authorization. Experience securing cross-service communication is a bonus - Experience with large-scale, customer-facing backend systems and enterprise-grade security - Clear communication and a real enjoyment of working with developers - A track record of owning delivery end to end Bonus: - Security for AI and LLM applications - Cloud-native experience (AWS or GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, IAM, networking, Linux internals) - Experience in regulated environments (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI, HIPAA) - Not required: Compliance certifications, incident response experience, a traditional security background, or prior domain knowledge. We care about what you have built and shipped, and open source work or conference talks are welcome evidence of that. LOCATION This role is remote and can be executed globally. However, to facilitate working with the Security Team, we prefer candidates based in GMT to GMT+3 or UK. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Dublin, London or Warsaw We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

items.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Consumer
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We're a small zero-to-one team at Anthropic building brand new consumer AI products. Our mandate: put the full power of frontier Claude models in people's hands, in products that don't exist yet. You'd be a founding engineer, and engineers here own products end to end. You won't be handed a spec. You'll come up with the bet, shape a vague idea into the leanest real version one, and ship it. Most zero-to-one bets don't work the first time, so you'll keep pushing new products over the line. If you'd rather have a clear spec and a stable surface, that's a valid preference. It's just not this team. Claude is already one of the most-used AI products in the world. What we build shapes how millions of people use AI every day. The pace is fast and the products are new. If you love building consumer products from scratch and care about getting the details right, we'd like to hear from you. Key responsibilities Originate new consumer AI product bets and own them from first idea to launch Spot the gap between what Claude can do and what people actually experience, and bring the bet: what to build, why now, and the cheapest way to test it Take a vague direction and cut it down to the leanest real version one Set technical direction for the products you build Own the quality bar for how the product looks and feels, treating latency, responsiveness, and reliability as first-class concerns Partner with privacy, security, legal, design, platform teams and external partners to find a path to launch Iterate quickly based on user feedback and internal testing Keep pushing new products over the line, since most zero-to-one bets don't work the first time Minimum qualifications Experience building consumer-facing products, with a strong emphasis on product quality and user experience Experience taking a consumer product from nothing to real users Proficiency in React, Next.js, and TypeScript Backend experience with Node.js Preferred qualifications 5+ years of experience building consumer-facing products, with a strong emphasis on product quality and user experience Experience founding a company, being on a founding team, or being an early engineer on a new consumer product Experience with products that have real-time or streaming interactions (chat interfaces, live updates) Experience optimizing performance for consumer web apps, from bundle size and rendering to end-to-end latency High agency: you pick a bet and own it without a roadmap Relentlessness: you keep going when a bet fails, verify instead of assume, and stay curious rather than frustrated Product taste: you care a lot about product craft, and you know what you'd refuse to ship Unusually high EQ: you understand other teams' constraints, seek out collaborations that create value for both sides, and can work with any team at Anthropic Willingness to pick up slack, even if it goes outside your job description The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Defense Success Manager, France
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes. Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support. This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job. You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them): - Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing. - Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.
