items.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity's security team protects products used by millions of people and thousands of enterprises, including AI agents that browse the web, run code, and act in customer systems. The team is small, senior, and builds most of what it uses: our own detections, agents that triage and investigate alerts around the clock, continuous offensive testing, and secure-by-default platforms for the rest of engineering. We're also turning what we've built into cybersecurity products for customers, so the same team that defends Perplexity builds what we ship. We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead and grow Security Engineering, including the engineers building our cybersecurity products. You'll own the team's execution and people, set the technical direction for how we defend our infrastructure, products, and corporate environment, and lead the product engineering work that brings those systems to customers. You'll stay close enough to the work to run an incident or review a design yourself. You'll report to Perplexity's head of security and work with engineering, infrastructure, IT, product, legal, and our co-founders. RESPONSIBILITIES - Lead, hire, and grow a team of security engineers across detection and response, cloud and infrastructure security, application and product security, offensive security, and identity and corporate security. - Lead the engineers building our cybersecurity products: set technical direction for agent-driven products across application security, offensive testing, cloud security, and detection and response, and own delivery to design partners and enterprise customers. - Keep the internal security program and the product tightly linked, so what the team runs on Perplexity every day becomes what we ship, and customer feedback improves how we defend ourselves. - Set the roadmap for Security Engineering, balancing incident load, risk reduction, and long-term platform investments, and make clear prioritization calls. - Own security incident response operations: on-call health, escalation, cross-team coordination during incidents, and postmortems that lead to real fixes. - Drive an AI-first security program. Push the team to automate investigation, response, and remediation with agents, and hold that automation to a high bar for accuracy and safety. - Partner with engineering and infrastructure leaders to get security work into their roadmaps, from threat models and design reviews to least-privilege access and secure-by-default libraries. - Represent Security Engineering in enterprise customer security reviews, external researcher and bug bounty engagements, and audits. - Build the team's operating rhythm: clear ownership, metrics that matter (time to detect, time to contain, open risk), and written standards others can follow. - Stay hands-on: review designs and code, run investigations when needed, and keep a working understanding of the systems the team defends. QUALIFICATIONS - 8+ years of engineering experience in security, with at least 3 years managing security or infrastructure engineering teams. - Deep hands-on background in at least two of: detection and response, cloud security (AWS preferred), application or product security, offensive security, or identity and access management. - Experience leading incident response for serious security incidents, including technical investigation, containment, and communication with executives and customers. - Strong management practice: clear feedback, effective 1:1s, career development, and a track record of hiring and retaining strong senior engineers. - Comfortable with modern infrastructure (Kubernetes, cloud-native services, CI/CD) and able to engage credibly with engineers on design and code. - Ability to make good tradeoffs under pressure and explain risk clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. - Experience shipping software products to external customers, ideally security products, including working with design partners and turning customer feedback into a roadmap. - Experience building security programs at a fast-growing company, where you built more than you bought. - Bonus: experience securing AI/ML systems, LLM applications, or autonomous agents, or using AI to scale security operations. - Bonus: experience supporting enterprise compliance programs (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) from the engineering side.

items.title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience. About the Role We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows. This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale. You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees. We’re looking for someone with: - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail. - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows. - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance. - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures. - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination. - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results. - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations. In this role, you will: - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements. - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue. - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues. - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions. - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners. - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability. - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands. - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership. You might thrive in this role if you: - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions. - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements. - Understand how invoices, approvals, supplier records, payment instructions, bank status, settlement, and reconciliation fit together, and can investigate discrepancies across them. - Bring a strong controls mindset aligned to SOX, including practical judgment on bank-detail changes, duplicate prevention, segregation of duties, reconciliation, and close support. - Have designed or improved ERP/AP payment workflows and bank integrations, including host-to-host automation, with tested controls and measurable results. - Have led teams or BPO partners through clear expectations, coaching, capacity planning, and sustained improvements in service and quality. - Communicate clearly with suppliers, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and can resolve issues across teams without losing ownership. - Are willing to work directly in payment queues, investigate failures, and support close when needed. - Experience with Oracle Fusion, Zip, or comparable integrated finance systems, and practical use of AI in controlled finance workflows, would be helpful. items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Web Access Engineer, Search Crawler)
items.description: Perplexity is hiring a Web Access Engineer for the Crawler team to build reliable fetching and rendering systems for AI-powered search. You'll work on freely available public web content, within site permissions and approved access policies, and develop the infrastructure that supplies content to downstream indexing and retrieval systems. Your focus will be diagnosing network errors, page-loading issues, and incomplete rendering. You'll trace problems from network protocols through client-side execution, distinguish technical failures from intentional access restrictions, and turn findings into production fixes that improve content quality and efficiency at scale. Responsibilities - Own fetching and rendering improvements end to end, from investigation through implementation and production rollout, partnering with crawler engineers and SREs. - Investigate fetch and rendering failures across DNS, TLS, HTTP, caching, redirects, and client-side rendering, and classify root causes. - Improve page loading, completion detection, and content capture to preserve relevant content and handle dynamic pages reliably. - Ensure the crawler respects site-imposed access restrictions and rate limits, identifies itself clearly, and retries only transient technical errors. - Build tools to reproduce failures, compare crawler output against expected page content, and turn findings into regression tests. - Define metrics for fetching reliability, content completeness, and error classification, and use them to prioritize improvements. Qualifications - 5+ years of software engineering experience in web infrastructure, browsers, CDNs, or crawling, with strong programming skills in at least one of Go, Python, Rust, or C++. - Deep understanding of HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3, including status semantics, caching, conditional requests, content encoding, and redirects; strong knowledge of TLS, DNS, cookies, and sessions. - Understanding of CDN caching and content delivery, HTTP error handling, retry backoff, and server-defined rate limits. - Knowledge of page lifecycle, network idle, service workers, client-side rendering, and shadow DOM; experience debugging JavaScript and fluency with Chrome DevTools, CDP, HAR files, curl, and packet captures. - Comfort working independently when the path forward is not fully defined. Nice to have - Experience developing CDN, caching, or web performance systems. - Experience operating crawlers, headless browsers, or distributed content-acquisition systems at scale. - Contributions to a browser engine or JavaScript runtime.

items.title: Head of Pipeline Operations
items.location_text: San Francisco, Austin, New York City
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our enterprise marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. We've grown this far without a marketing automation platform or a dedicated Pipeline Operations team. We're ready to build both. We're hiring our first Head of Pipeline Operations. You'll choose and implement our first marketing automation platform, own how every marketing and product lead is enriched and routed, and work with Data Science and Growth on how MQLs and PQLs are scored and qualified. You'll own the systems our BDR team prospects in and co-own execution support with BDR leadership. And you'll build the campaign operations, attribution and reporting that connect B2B and enterprise marketing to pipeline and revenue. You'll report to the Head of Revenue Operations and build a team. Your first direct report is a GTM Engineer, who owns our enrichment platform, lead routing and warehouse-to-Salesforce syncs. You set the definitions and priorities, and the GTM Engineer is your force multiplier for delivering them. Tech stack: Salesforce | Snowflake | Clay | Marketing automation (you'll choose it) | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Computer WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious. - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it. - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users. - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products. - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build and lead the Pipeline Operations team. Manage the GTM Engineer from day one, set the roadmap, and hire as the function grows. Stay hands-on while the team is small. - Select and implement our marketing automation platform. Run the evaluation, then lead the rollout: data model, lifecycle stages, templates, permissions and migration of existing B2B email programs. - Own the lead lifecycle. Define lifecycle stages, qualification criteria, handoff SLAs and recycle rules with Marketing and Sales leadership, and enforce them consistently across our systems. - Own enrichment and routing, and make scoring drive action. You are accountable for every lead being complete and sent to nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager within SLA, and you direct the GTM Engineer who runs these systems. Data Science owns our scoring models, including product-qualified lead scoring. On marketing-qualified lead scoring, you represent Marketing and Sales: define what qualifies, supply engagement signals and agree handoff thresholds. - Run product-qualified leads in parallel with marketing-qualified leads. PQLs flow to BDRs too. Work with Growth, who publish the product usage signals behind them, and Data Science, who score them, on how PQLs are qualified, routed and followed up, with the same lifecycle, SLAs and reporting as MQLs. - Own BDR systems, and co-own execution support with BDR leadership. You own the infrastructure: the sequencing, dialing and research tools, the Salesforce lead and account queues, and the integrations between them. Lead the implementation and evolution of this toolset, a combination of internally built applications and vendor solutions, with the GTM Engineer and our GTM Platform team delivering the builds. BDR leadership takes the primary role in daily and weekly use: building sequences and plays, activating target lists, actioning signals and monitoring SLAs on routed leads. They own the substance inside the systems and the business results across their team. You own resolving system and data issues, and reporting activity by rep and by play. - Stand up account-based marketing and sales as a motion. With Sales and Marketing leadership, select and tier target accounts by fit, intent and product usage, using the account fit scores Data Science publishes, and set the investment for each tier. Map buying groups and work with Data Science on an account-level engagement score that tells BDRs and AEs when to act. Design coordinated plays across email, ads, events and outbound, with clear triggers, owners and SLAs. Measure by account: coverage, engagement, meetings, pipeline and win rate against non-target accounts. - Own nurture and campaign infrastructure for B2B and enterprise marketing, and co-own execution with Marketing. You own the build: nurture enrollment rules, segments, templates, tracking, QA, a repeatable launch process and a clean Salesforce campaign structure. Marketing takes the primary role in what runs through it: strategy, audiences, offers, content, calendar and budget. They own the substance of the programs and the pipeline they produce. You own launching on schedule and reporting performance by program. - Own attribution and marketing reporting. Build the tracking and lead source model, define how we measure marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline, and own the dashboards and weekly funnel review. Marketing and Revenue Operations should report the same numbers. - Protect consent and deliverability. Own consent, suppression and sending-domain health for B2B and enterprise marketing email, and agree shared rules on contact frequency and sending domains with Growth, who own product and consumer lifecycle messaging. - Partner with Growth on web conversion. Growth owns the website and sign-up flows. You own what happens to a B2B lead after capture: form fields, tracking, consent and a clean handoff into our systems. - Own the marketing technology stack, its budget and the team's operating rhythm. Evaluate vendors and manage renewals. Run intake and prioritization, document every system, and use Computer and other AI tools so a small team does more. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In your first 30 days: - Audit how leads are captured, enriched, scored, routed, emailed and worked by BDRs today, and document the gaps. - Write the marketing automation platform requirements and start the evaluation. - Agree with Growth on who owns which messages, audiences and sending domains. - Set the GTM Engineer's priorities for enrichment, routing and syncs, and publish a baseline funnel report. In your first 60 days: - Select the platform and start implementation. - Publish agreed lifecycle stage definitions and handoff SLAs. - Agree MQL and PQL qualification criteria and handoff thresholds with Data Science, Growth and Sales. - Agree a BDR systems roadmap and support model with BDR leadership, and publish baseline activity and meeting reporting by rep and by play. In your first 120 days: - Take the platform live with a reliable Salesforce sync, consent management and the first nurture programs built and launched with Marketing. - Have enrichment and routing meet the agreed speed-to-lead SLA, with scores and their reasons visible to reps in Salesforce. - Deliver a first attribution model that Marketing, Sales and Finance all use. In your first 6 months: - Start building the team beyond the GTM Engineer, on a hiring plan you've made the case for. - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion for both MQLs and PQLs. - Report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline as one trusted number in company planning. QUALIFICATIONS - 8+ years in marketing operations or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including 2+ years managing people. - Experience at a company with a large consumer user base alongside an enterprise business, in a hybrid product-led and sales-led motion. You've coordinated with a product lifecycle or growth team on product-qualified leads and mapping users to accounts. - You've led the selection and implementation of a marketing automation platform from scratch, or a full migration, including the Salesforce sync. You can still build in a major platform, such as HubSpot or Marketo, yourself. - You've designed, shipped and measured lead routing, with a lifecycle and SLAs that Sales followed. - You've set lead scoring criteria and thresholds with a data science or analytics team, and can judge whether a score is working. - You've been the operations partner to a BDR or SDR team, running their sequencing and dialing tools, lead queues and reporting while sales development leaders ran the plays. - You've built attribution and pipeline reporting that Sales and Finance used to make decisions. - You've directed technical builders, such as GTM engineers or analysts, and can scope their work and judge the result. - Working knowledge of the Salesforce data model, privacy rules (GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM) and email deliverability, and enough SQL to trace a record across systems. - Clear communicator and builder. You explain systems and data to executives without jargon, and you're comfortable being the first hire in a function. NICE TO HAVE Experience with: - A warehouse-first stack: Snowflake, dbt, reverse ETL and Clay. - AI-native marketing tools or agents deployed in production. - Event and webinar operations, including lead capture and follow-up.

The Government Products team focuses on building and scaling systems that support long-term investing and account management for millions of customers. What you bring 5+ years of professional software development experience. 3+ years of experience building low-latency, large-scale distributed systems in production environments. items.title: Integrated Marketing Manager - Consumer & Brand, LATAM
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s LATAM Marketing team helps people understand how AI can benefit their lives and put that value into practice. We connect global product innovation with local consumer needs, culture and behavior across Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America, contributing to OpenAI’s mission of ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We build the ChatGPT brand through integrated campaigns, creator and social programs, partnerships and cultural experiences. We work with local and global teams to make ChatGPT relevant and useful in people’s everyday lives. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a hands-on Integrated Marketing Manager to lead Consumer and Brand campaigns across LATAM. The role is based in São Paulo and works closely with regional and global teams. You’ll turn consumer and cultural insights into a clear brief and a distinctive creative idea that shows why ChatGPT matters in people’s everyday lives. You’ll lead the work from strategy through production and launch, and build ongoing marketing programs that keep the brand relevant from always on to major campaigns. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Define the audience, cultural insight, brand objective and role for marketing in each program. - Write clear creative briefs, guide concept development and give actionable feedback to internal creative teams and external partners. - Own integrated consumer campaigns from brief through launch and measurement. Give paid, owned and earned media, social, creators, partnerships and experiences partners distinct roles in bringing the campaign idea to life. - Develop locally originated campaigns and adapt global work for Brazil and other LATAM markets without losing the core brand strategy. - Build and run ongoing consumer marketing programs around cultural moments and everyday needs. Set priorities, clarify who owns the work and use each campaign’s learnings to improve the program over time. - Align local, regional and global partners on the campaign brief, channel roles and the decisions needed to deliver the work. - Work with Creative, Production, Comms, Media and regional teams to make decisions and deliver on time. Partner with Product Marketing and Growth when a campaign depends on product claims or activation. - Set campaign goals and a practical measurement plan up front, then use brand and channel results to improve the next round of work. - Manage campaign resources,external partners, budgets and production dependencies within agreed authority; make clear trade-offs and build forward plans that account for creative lead times and local market conditions. WHAT YOU BRING - 12+ years of technology marketing experience across Brazil and Spanish-speaking LATAM. You’ve led major tech consumer brand campaigns and ongoing integrated marketing programs from brief through results. - Deep knowledge of LATAM consumers, culture and media, and the ability to turn that knowledge into a clear strategic choice. - Strong creative judgment and experience leading the briefing, concept review and production process with internal teams and agencies. - A record of bringing a compelling consumer product idea to life through brand strategy, local insight and distinctive creative work. - Experience developing channel plans across paid, owned and earned media, social, creators, partnerships or experiences. - Comfort defining brand and campaign success, interpreting measurement with specialist partners and turning results into practical decisions. - Experience balancing regional consistency with local nuance, and influencing cross-functional and global teams without relying on formal authority. - A clear record of personal ownership and autonomy: you can set direction, produce high-quality work directly, manage external partners, delivery, and make progress with incomplete inputs and limited resources. - Professional fluency in Portuguese and English. items.title: Growth GTM Engineer, Revenue Operations
items.location_text: San Francisco, Austin, New York City
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. To turn that demand into pipeline, every lead has to be enriched, scored, and routed to the right next step within minutes. We're hiring a Growth GTM Engineer on the Revenue Operations team to own the lead-to-engagement engine: the enrichment platform that completes every marketing and product lead, the routing that sends each lead to nurture or to BDRs and Sales, and the syncs that move data from our warehouse into Salesforce and our GTM tools. You'll also put lead and account scores to work with Data Science, who own the scoring models, and help deliver our BDRs' prospecting tools. You'll report to the Head of Pipeline Operations, who sets the priorities for this work and owns our marketing automation platform, campaign operations and attribution. You'll build mostly with AI, so we care more about your instinct for go-to-market systems than your depth in any one programming language. You'll measure everything you build against meetings, pipeline and revenue. Tech stack: Salesforce | Clay | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Snowflake | SQL | Python | Computer | LLM APIs WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious. - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it. - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users. - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products. - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the enrichment platform. Design and run waterfall enrichment across third-party providers, AI research agents and first-party data for every marketing and product lead. Handle lead-to-account matching, deduplication, field governance, data freshness and provider cost. Publish enriched data to the warehouse for Data Science and other teams to use. - Own lead routing. Design the decision logic that sends each lead, from marketing programs or product usage, to Marketing for nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager for engagement, based on score, segment, territory, account ownership, capacity and existing opportunities. Co-define lifecycle stages, handoff SLAs, recycle rules and speed-to-lead triggers with the Head of Pipeline Operations, and enforce them in Salesforce and our routing tools, with MQLs and PQLs on the same lifecycle and SLAs. Deliver the enrichment, signals, routing and alerts behind our account-based plays. - Own the syncs between our warehouse and our GTM tools. Build and maintain the reverse ETL syncs, APIs and webhooks that move data from Snowflake into Salesforce, marketing automation, routing and engagement tools. Build on the models the Data team publishes, and make sure every synced field has one owner and every sync is monitored. Support the rollout of our first marketing automation platform by building its Salesforce sync and warehouse feeds, along with the nurture enrollment rules and campaign tracking the Head of Pipeline Operations designs. - Put lead and account scores to work. Data Science owns our scoring models, including product-qualified lead scoring. Partner with them on marketing-qualified lead scoring by bringing in enrichment data, marketing engagement and Sales feedback, and help set the thresholds that trigger action. Make sure scores and their reasons reach Salesforce on time and that Sales understands them. - Close the feedback loop. Track the funnel from lead creation to closed-won. Find where leads stall, which sources and signals predict pipeline, and whether our qualification criteria still hold, then feed that back into routing, Marketing programs and Data Science's scoring work. Capture the campaign and touchpoint data behind attribution, which the Head of Pipeline Operations owns. - Help deliver the BDR prospecting toolset. It combines vendor solutions and internal applications. The Head of Pipeline Operations owns these systems, and BDR leadership decides the sequences and plays that run on them. Implement the vendor tools and integrate them with Salesforce and our data. Build the workflows and agents around them, such as signal-triggered alerts, prioritized outreach queues and pre-call research briefs. Resolve the system and data issues that slow reps down. Supply our GTM Platform team, which builds our rep-facing applications, with the data, signals and requirements they need. Talk to users, track adoption and retire what doesn't get used. - Partner across the business. Work with Marketing, Growth, BDR and Sales leadership, Data Science, Data Engineering, GTM Platform and Sales Systems to turn messy processes into durable systems, and use the scores and product usage signals Data Science and Growth publish to drive routing. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In your first 30 days: - Audit enrichment coverage, routing rules, warehouse-to-Salesforce syncs and lead SLAs, and document the gaps that cost us pipeline. In your first 60 days: - Ship an enrichment waterfall with measurable gains in fill rate and accuracy. - Ship routing that sends every marketing and product lead to nurture or sales within an agreed SLA, with dashboards for speed to lead and conversion by route. - Take ownership of the syncs that write scores and lead fields to Salesforce, with monitoring and one owner per field. - Work with Data Science to bring enrichment and marketing engagement data into MQL scoring. In your first 90 days: - Ship at least one prospecting workflow or agent with sustained weekly use by BDRs and AEs. - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion for both MQLs and PQLs. QUALIFICATIONS - 4+ years in GTM engineering, RevOps or Marketing Ops engineering, growth engineering, or data engineering in B2B SaaS, including 2+ years building enrichment, routing or integration systems. - Commercial instinct. You start from a revenue problem and work back to the data, logic or tool that fixes it. - Working SQL. You pull your own data from a warehouse (Snowflake or similar) and build on the models other teams publish. - AI-first builder. You've shipped integrations, automations or agents that real users depend on, using AI coding tools, and you can read, review and debug what you ship. Language depth matters less than GTM judgment. - Deep working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns, ownership), and experience automating and integrating with it. - Hands-on experience with enrichment and intent tools (Clay, ZoomInfo, Apollo, 6sense, Common Room or similar), routing and scheduling tools (Default, Chili Piper, LeanData) and reverse ETL (Hightouch, Census). - Fluency with funnel mechanics: lifecycle design, routing logic, score thresholds, SLAs, attribution data and conversion metrics. - Comfort with REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, rate limits and error handling. - Operator mindset. You work directly with reps and marketers, ship fixes quickly, and don't need a PM to translate requests. NICE TO HAVE - Hybrid PLG and sales-led motions: product-qualified leads, user-to-account mapping and sales-assist routing. - LLM-powered research, personalization or qualification agents, including evaluation and monitoring. - Working alongside a data science team on lead or account scoring. - dbt, or production work in Python or TypeScript. - Entity resolution and domain matching at scale. - A prior GTM Engineer role at a GTM-tooling or AI-native company.

items.title: Partner Director, IBM North America
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem to accelerate customer success, enable responsible enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers. Global systems integrators and technology services partners help enterprises move from AI strategy to production deployment. This role will lead OpenAI’s co-sell initiatives with IBM across North America, bringing together IBM’s consulting, technology, industry, and delivery capabilities with OpenAI’s products and platform. You will turn the global partnership strategy into a focused North America sales plan and repeatable field execution that delivers customer and commercial impact. About the Role We are hiring a Partner Sales Director to own IBM’s North America co-sell execution and measurable contribution to OpenAI growth. You will translate the global IBM partnership strategy into a prioritized regional business plan, activate IBM and OpenAI account teams, and drive qualified pipeline, closed business and sustained production adoption in partnership with sales, technical and delivery leaders. The role owns North America account prioritization, field activation, pursuit orchestration and partner forecasting within the global plan. Global partnership strategy, cross-region programs and commercial frameworks remain with global leadership; customer account ownership remains with the relevant OpenAI sales teams. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will connect senior executive engagement with joint account planning, co-selling, solution and delivery alignment, field enablement, governance, and day-to-day execution. Success requires a strong understanding of how a large, matrixed services and technology organization operates, commercial discipline, technical fluency, and the ability to align teams without formal authority. The ideal candidate has led a high-impact partnership with IBM, built measurable pipeline and customer outcomes across North America, and knows how to turn partnership GTM strategy into account-level execution and successful deployments. In this role, you will: - Own North America partner sales and GTM with IBM, including regional strategy, executive alignment, joint planning, pipeline growth, customer outcomes, delivery-readiness coordination and escalation, and long-term expansion, in alignment with the global alliance. - Develop and execute a North America joint business plan with clear account and industry priorities, investments, decision rights, milestones, and measures of success. - Build trusted relationships across IBM Consulting, IBM Technology, North America industry and regional leadership, alliance teams, client account leaders, sales organizations, architects, and delivery leaders, while staying aligned with global stakeholders. - Translate executive priorities into repeatable field execution spanning account mapping, opportunity qualification, co-selling, solution development, technical engagement, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Shape joint solutions and industry plays that combine OpenAI capabilities with IBM’s consulting, technology, hybrid cloud, data, security, governance, and delivery strengths. - Lead joint account planning and strategic customer pursuits with IBM and OpenAI field teams across North America, with particular focus on complex and regulated enterprises. - Create a clear engagement model for OpenAI sellers and technical teams, including when to involve IBM, how opportunities are qualified, who owns each step, and how channel conflict is resolved. - Partner with Product, Engineering, Solutions, Security, Legal, Finance, and Commercial teams to support complex customer engagements and remove technical, contractual, compliance, and operational blockers. - Build IBM’s North America field and delivery readiness through executive sponsorship, sales enablement, technical training, reusable solution patterns, and disciplined delivery handoffs. - Establish regional governance across executive business reviews, pipeline inspection, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation, connected to the global alliance operating model. - Own and track agreed North America commercial targets across qualified partner-sourced and co-sell pipeline, conversion to closed business, OpenAI revenue or consumption, and production adoption, with clear attribution and no double counting. - Align resource priorities with OpenAI sales and technical leaders for North America opportunities with the greatest strategic value, commercial potential, customer impact, delivery readiness, and repeatability. - Represent OpenAI in senior partner, customer, and industry engagements with clarity, sound judgment, and strong executive presence. - Build the regional operating model and identify the team capacity needed to scale the IBM partnership across North America. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Significant experience leading strategic alliances, GSI, or advisory partnerships, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise go-to-market programs in AI, cloud, data, SaaS, or enterprise technology. - Direct experience working with IBM and deep familiarity with its North America organization, consulting and technology businesses, incentives, decision-making networks, commercial model, and enterprise delivery motions. - A proven record of turning a strategic partnership into a qualified pipeline, closed business and production adoption, with clear evidence of your contribution to the commercial results. - Experience designing and scaling joint operating models across large, matrixed organizations, including governance, account planning, incentives, staffing, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Demonstrated success shaping and advancing complex C-suite enterprise transformation opportunities from strategy through production deployment. - Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility with senior IBM and customer leaders while remaining close to operating details. - Commercial judgment and experience prioritizing investments, qualifying opportunities, managing forecasts, and making clear tradeoffs. - Technical fluency across enterprise AI, cloud and hybrid environments, data platforms, integration, security, governance, risk, and modern application architectures. - Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to align Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, and Operations without direct authority. - Experience building partner enablement, joint solutions, industry plays, and scalable field engagement models across North America. - Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure, accountability, and momentum in a rapidly evolving market. - Excellent written and verbal communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills. - A builder mindset, high ownership, low ego, and a consistent focus on customer value and responsible AI adoption. What success looks like - OpenAI and IBM have a clear North America growth strategy, differentiated joint value proposition, executive governance model, and measurable business plan aligned with the global alliance. - IBM and OpenAI field teams across North America know when and how to engage one another, and qualified opportunities progress through a consistent co-sell and delivery motion. - The North America partnership generates qualified pipeline and converts priority opportunities into secure, successful production deployments with demonstrable customer value. - Joint solution patterns and industry plays become repeatable rather than remaining bespoke. - OpenAI resources are allocated transparently toward the highest-impact opportunities. - IBM’s North America teams demonstrate growing readiness and accountability across selling, architecture, implementation, and customer success. - The North America partnership earns sustained executive sponsorship and delivers measurable year-over-year growth. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.
